answer: Bind each identity to one piece of physical mail: the network posts a single-use code to a street address, and only whoever receives it can claim the key. A farm must rent, receive and empty a separate mailbox per clone, paying real postage and real waiting time, so the cost cannot be pooled across a thousand names. The registry is a plain atlas of deliverable addresses, one entry each, and a duplicated address voids both claims. That is the haven: the post office, not the protocol, sets the mesa every clone has to climb.
